classifier_rationale: The merchant promised to refund the last month's dues after cancellation and the credit never posted.

retrieved.text: Merchant credit wait period. If the merchant's credit or refund is dated less than 10 business days ago, set the expectation and schedule a follow-up. If it's older, or a statement closed without it, open a billing-error dispute.

Written notice link. After a billing-error intake by phone, send the cardholder a link the same day to submit or confirm the dispute electronically. The cardholder's submission is the written notice under REG-03. The call alone is not. POL-04 does not apply to UN, because notice of unauthorized use can be by phone (REG-12).

Quality disputes (claims and defenses). A complaint about the quality of goods the cardholder accepted isn't a billing error. It may qualify as a claim against the issuer if the cardholder tried in good faith to resolve it with the merchant, the purchase was over $50, and it happened in the cardholder's state or within 100 miles of their address. The $50 and location limits don't apply when the merchant and issuer are related.

note: Cardholder cancelled a Peakform Gym membership at the end of August 2026. A charge posted 2026-08-31; amount and statement date not stated. A manager verbally promised the last month's dues would be refunded to the card within 7-10 business days. No credit has posted, and more than a month has passed. Cardholder called Peakform a couple of weeks ago and left two voicemails with no reply. Cardholder holds a printed cancellation form annotated that dues would be returned. Next action: OPEN_DISPUTE under POL-03, since the promised refund window has elapsed. Send the written-notice link the same day per POL-04. Unknown: amount, statement date, 60-day window status, whether written notice was already sent. No second issue raised.
